title: Presentation: You Can't Trust Your AI Bill. And Neither Can I
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-cloud-cost-economics/en/mediumimage/erik-peterson-medium-1791451373591.jpg"/><p>Erik Peterson discusses why AI spend is eclipsing cloud bills, triggering a major software engineering cost crisis. He explains tokenmaxxing, unit economics, forced developer promotions, and why fully autonomous AI will write, deploy, and govern code by 2028.</p> <i>By Erik Peterson</i>

title: GitLab 19.4 Adds Goal-Driven Agents and Tighter Cost Controls
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/gitlab-19-4-goal-driven-agents/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791743492913.jpg"/><p>GitLab has released version 19.4 of its DevSecOps platform, adding a goal-driven mode to GitLab Duo CLI, three hosted open-weight models, a larger set of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and more detailed controls for AI spending.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: Foresight AI Brings Gremlin Agents to Reliability Engineering
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/gremlin-foresight-ai/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791653267864.jpg"/><p>Reliability management company Gremlin has announced the general availability of Foresight AI, an agentic product that analyses services for potential failures, recommends changes and reruns tests to check that a fix works.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: AWS Introduces Enhanced Custom Event Buses for EventBridge
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-enhanced-eventbridge-buses/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790663976977.jpg"/><p>AWS recently announced enhanced custom event buses for Amazon EventBridge, allowing organizations to share a centralized bus across accounts with ordered delivery, simplified subscriber management, event replay, content-based deduplication, and a new publisher/subscriber-based pricing model.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Cloudflare Traces Turns the Proxy Layer into OpenTelemetry Spans, with New Volume-Based Pricing
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-traces-open-beta/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791443919168.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has put Traces into open beta, extending automatic tracing from Workers to security rules, transformations, cache, routing and origin handling as OpenTelemetry spans. Traces accept and forward W3C traceparent headers, and Trace Rules allow targeted sampling. Pricing moves to ingestion and retention volume from December 1.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: CircleCI Makes Machine Runner Orchestrator Generally Available
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/circleci-machine-runner/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790836191409.jpg"/><p>CircleCI has made its Machine Runner Orchestrator 1.0.0 generally available, providing automated scaling of self-hosted machine runner virtual machines according to CI workload demand.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: Ontology‐Driven Observability: Building the E2E Knowledge Graph at Netflix Scale
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/netflix-observability-aiops-ontology-scale/en/mediumimage/medium-1790845339712.jpg"/><p>Prasanna Vijayanathan and Renzo Sanchez-Silva share how Netflix tackles observability across 38M events/sec. They discuss replacing reactive monitoring with an AI-driven operational ontology and agentic workflows using Claude and graph databases. They explain how unifying MELT telemetry into queryable knowledge graphs enables automated triaging, root-cause analysis, and self-healing systems.</p> <i>By Prasanna Vijayanathan, Renzo Sanchez-Silva</i>

title: HashiCorp Relased Terraform Google Cloud Provider 8.0 in General Availability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/terraform-google-cloud-provider/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791470649216.jpg"/><p>HashiCorp has announced the general availability of version 8.0 of the Terraform provider for Google Cloud. The major release updates the default load balancing for two Compute Engine resources. It also removes resources linked to retired Google Cloud services.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: Cloudflare K2 Builds Event Streams on R2 Object Storage, at a Second of Produce Latency
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-k2-serverless-streams/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791040228747.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has launched K2 in public beta, a serverless event streaming service implementing a durable log on R2 object storage. Cloudflare states produce latency of about one second at p99; a tester reported end-to-end p99 of 7.5 seconds, which a commenter answering for the team said was higher than expected. Consume charges match produce charges per GB.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Presentation: The Reinvention of the Dev Team
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/agentic-dev-teams/en/mediumimage/medium-1790242915891.jpeg"/><p>Hannah Foxwell shares how the surge of agentic coding forces engineering leaders to rethink team dynamics. She discusses three key anchors for navigating AI-driven velocity: building software worth building, prioritizing automated safety over speed, and preserving the human element through generalist "broken comb" skillsets and sustainable on-call practices.</p> <i>By Hannah Foxwell</i>

title: Spanner Omni Reaches GA, Replacing Google's Atomic Clocks and File System with Software
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/spanner-omni-deploy-anywhere-ga/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791038786495.jpg"/><p>Google has made Spanner Omni generally available, running its distributed SQL database on-premises, across clouds or on a laptop. Doing so meant replacing Colossus with a Colossus-like abstraction layer and TrueTime with software-based time synchronization. There is no availability SLA, and practitioners are pricing the move in tail latency and operational toil.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: OpenTelemetry Makes Kubernetes Attributes Processor Stable as Observability Schema Matures
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/opentelemetry-kubernetes-observ/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790835749063.jpg"/><p>OpenTelemetry has promoted its Kubernetes Attributes Processor to v1.0.0, marking a significant step in making Kubernetes telemetry more predictable and stable across observability pipelines.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: Building Resilient Platforms: Insights from 20+ Years in Mission-Critical Infrastructure
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/infrastructure-financial-services-platform/en/mediumimage/medium-1790844962852.jpeg"/><p>Matthew Liste explains the 12 core principles of building scalable, reliable platforms for enterprise tech teams. From avoiding technical debt and managing deprecation to building a strong engineering culture, Liste discusses how to design infrastructure platforms that reduce complexity, streamline developer workflows, and deliver long-term value for senior architects and engineering leaders.</p> <i>By Matthew Liste</i>

title: Cloudflare Introduces CLI for AI Agents, Sunsetting Wrangler
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-cf-cli/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790917350141.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare recently launched the open beta of cf, a new open-source, agent-focused command-line interface for interacting with Cloudflare services through a unified CLI. Written in TypeScript, it provides structured output and command discovery to make Cloudflare’s APIs easier for both developers and AI agents.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Podcast: Future Cybersecurity: Hardware Memory Safety, Automated Governance and Post-Quantum Cryptography
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/future-cybersecurity-hardware-memory-safety/en/smallimage/infoq-podcast-500-1790672981256.jpg"/><p>In this episode, Chris Swan, engineer at Atsign and security track host at QCon London, reflects on the ideas shared during QCon London 2026 and teases topics of the future edition. The discussion explores how security engineering is shifting from relying on human vigilance toward automated, system-level defences across the entire application stack.</p> <i>By Chris Swan</i>
